3.1.indicator: Institutional and sectoral coordination across agencies and jurisdictions
3.1.evidence:
For the purpose of organizing, monitoring and improving coordinated and efficient protection, the body or institution referred to in Article 5 paragraph 1 of this Law may form a team of experts from the fields of social and child protection, health protection, justice, police protection, protection of human rights and freedoms, as well as representatives of non-governmental organizations dealing with protection.
The bodies and institutions from paragraph 1 of this Article are obliged to give priority, in accordance with the law, to resolving cases of violence and to ensure mutual notification and assistance in order to prevent and detect violence, eliminate causes and provide assistance to the victim in establishing conditions for a safe life.
3.1.rationale: The framework provides for multi-agency coordination by allowing formation of an expert team drawing from multiple sectors (social/child protection, health, justice, police, human rights, NGOs) for organizing/monitoring/improving coordinated protection, and it also requires mutual notification and assistance among relevant bodies and institutions to prevent/detect violence and assist victims. This goes beyond assigning isolated responsibilities and constitutes an operative coordination mechanism/process.
3.1.evidence_original:
Radi organizovanja, praćenja i unaprjeđenja koordinirane i efikasne zaštite organ ili ustanova iz člana 5 stav 1 ovog zakona može obrazovati tim od stručnjaka iz oblasti socijalne i dječje zaštite, zdravstvene zaštite, pravosuđa, policijske zaštite, zaštite ljudskih prava i sloboda, kao i predstavnika nevladinih organizacija koje se bave zaštitom.

Organi i ustanove iz stava 1 ovog člana dužni su da u skladu sa zakonom daju prioritet rješavanju slučajeva nasilja i obezbijede međusobno obavještavanje i pomoć radi sprečavanja i otkrivanja nasilja, otklanjanja uzroka i pružanja pomoći žrtvi u uspostavljanju uslova za bezbjedan život.

3.2.rationale: The framework explicitly requires authorities and institutions to keep records on reported violence cases, victims, perpetrators, and protective measures, and to submit those records to a designated ministry. This assigns responsibility for recording and reporting case data, meeting the substantive threshold.
